crywolf: Bayesian false-positive occupancy models with calibration checks

Source: R/crywolf-package.R
crywolf-package.Rd

Automated detectors, such as acoustic classifiers, return false positives, and occupancy models that ignore them overestimate occupancy and distort covariate effects. crywolf fits the multiple-methods (site-confirmation) false-positive occupancy model of Miller et al. (2011), in which a subset of detections is verified and therefore certain, and asks whether the correction is calibrated for a given study design.

The package has three parts:

  • Data and model. fp_data() (or fp_data_wide()) assembles the detections, and fp_occu() fits the model in Stan through 'cmdstanr'. The false-positive rate can be constant (fp = ~ 1) or depend on site covariates (fp = ~ w), with an optional site random effect (random_fp = TRUE), and the true-detection process accepts observation covariates and a recorder random effect. The observation-confirmation design of Chambert et al. (2015), in which an expert checks the detections of some automated occasions, is supported through the confirmed argument of fp_data(). fp_read_birdnet(), fp_read_validation(), and fp_aggregate() build the data from classifier output, and curiango holds a real dataset.

  • Checking and plotting. fp_prior_predictive() checks the priors against the data, fp_ppc() runs a posterior predictive check, and plot.fp_occu(), fp_effects(), and fp_sites() show the coefficients, the effect of a covariate, and the probability that each site is occupied.

  • Simulation. simulate_fp() generates data under homogeneous, unstructured, and structured ("confusion") false-positive regimes.

  • Calibration. fp_calibrate() and fp_verification_curve() fit the model to many simulated datasets and report the coverage of the 95% credible intervals and the bias of the quantities of interest, so that users can see whether the correction holds for their design and how much verification it needs.

Installation

crywolf is distributed through R-universe, with binaries for Windows, macOS, and Linux. 'cmdstanr' comes from the Stan R-universe, and CmdStan itself is installed once:

install.packages("crywolf", repos = c("https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev",
                                      "https://stan-dev.r-universe.dev",
                                      getOption("repos")))
cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()

The model is compiled the first time fp_occu() needs it, or ahead of time with fp_compile(), and the executable is kept in the user cache directory for later sessions.

Getting started

vignette("crywolf") introduces the model and the workflow. Further articles cover simulation (vignette("simulation")), calibration and how much to verify (vignette("calibration")), a case study with real data (vignette("curiango")), the translation from 'unmarked' (vignette("unmarked")), and the Stan program (vignette("stan_model")). They are also on the package website, https://provetelab.org/crywolf/.

Model

For site \(i\), automated occasion \(k\), and verified occasion \(m\): $$z_i \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(\psi_i), \quad \mathrm{logit}(\psi_i) = X_i\beta$$ $$y^{aut}_{ik} \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(z_i p_{11,ik} + (1 - z_i) p_{10,i})$$ $$\mathrm{logit}(p_{11,ik}) = Z_{ik}\alpha + u_{j[ik]}, \quad \mathrm{logit}(p_{10,i}) = \alpha_1 - \Delta + W_i\gamma$$ $$y^{ver}_{im} \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(z_i r_{11})$$ The latent state \(z\) is marginalized. The positive gap \(\Delta\) keeps the true-detection probability above the false-positive probability at the reference values of the covariates, which prevents label switching. Priors are Normal on the logit scale for intercepts and slopes, Normal truncated at zero for \(\Delta\), and half-Normal for the standard deviations of the random effects; fp_priors() lists the defaults and changes them without recompiling. vignette("stan_model") walks through the Stan program.

Computation

Each chain runs on one core by default. The likelihood is summed over sites with Stan's reduce_sum(), so threads_per_chain in fp_occu() splits each chain among several cores, which pays off with many sites or occasions. Keep parallel_chains * threads_per_chain at or below the number of physical cores. fp_calibrate() fits many models, one chain per worker; compile the model with fp_compile() before starting workers.

Citation

citation("crywolf") gives the reference to the package. Every release is archived on Zenodo; doi:10.5281/zenodo.23385045 always resolves to the latest version.

References

Miller, D. A., Nichols, J. D., McClintock, B. T., Grant, E. H. C., Bailey, L. L., & Weir, L. A. (2011). Improving occupancy estimation when two types of observational error occur: non-detection and species misidentification. Ecology, 92, 1422–1428. doi:10.1890/10-1396.1

Chambert, T., Miller, D. A. W., & Nichols, J. D. (2015). Modeling false positive detections in species occurrence data under different study designs. Ecology, 96, 332–339. doi:10.1890/14-1507.1
